title: [C16T3] Airport Site Development
prompt: The plans show the site of an airport now and how it will look after redevelopment next year. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The diagrams illustrate the current layout of Southwest Airport and its planned redevelopment that will be completed next year.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, while the basic structure with separate areas for departures and arrivals will be maintained, the airport will be significantly expanded with more gates and additional facilities. The most notable change is the extension of the walkway system to accommodate more than twice the number of gates.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: At the entrance, the airport has two separate sections. The left section houses departures, featuring security and passport control facilities, along with check-in counters and a café in the departures area. After redevelopment, this section will gain a new bag drop zone while retaining its café and other current facilities. In the right section, which handles arrivals, there are passport control and customs areas. This section will be enhanced with new ATM machines and car hire services.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Moving to the upper portion of the airport, two parallel walkways currently connect to eight boarding gates. In the redevelopment plan, this simple configuration will be transformed into a Y-shaped terminal with branching walkways serving 18 gates. A sky train will also be added to transport passengers throughout the expanded terminal.
